We are seeking a highly skilled and experienced Senior Air Quality Consultant to join our team. The ideal candidate will have extensive experience with the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) and regulatory compliance (reporting and permitting). This role involves managing complex air quality projects, ensuring compliance with environmental regulations, and providing expert guidance to clients.

Lead and manage air quality assessments and impact analyses for various projects.
Ensure compliance with CEQA and other relevant environmental regulations.
Prepare and review technical reports, including air quality impact assessments and mitigation plans.
Conduct air quality modeling and data analysis.
Provide expert advice and support to clients on air quality issues and regulatory requirements.
Complete air quality permits under SCAQMD, SJVAPCD, BAAQMD and other Air Districts, including Title V Permits
Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to develop and implement air quality management strategies.
Stay updated on the latest developments in air quality regulations and best practices.
Mentor and train junior staff members.

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, or a related field.

Strong knowledge of air quality regulations, including CEQA, the Clean Air Act, and local air district rules.
Proficiency in air quality modeling software (e.g., AERMOD, CalEEMod).
Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and project management skills.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
Professional certifications (e.g., CPP, QEP, PE) are a plus.

FMC Corporation is a global leader in agricultural sciences, driven by our purpose: Innovation for Agriculture. Solutions for the Planet. With one of the most productive and diversified pipelines in the industry, FMC is delivering cutting-edge and next-generation crop protection technologies – including Dodhylex™ active, Isoflex™ active, rimisoxafen, and fluindapyr – to help farmers increase the productivity and resilience of their land. From day one, you’ll contribute to meaningful work that drives progress in agriculture, supported by a culture that values integrity, safety, respect, and results. Join us in advancing the future of agriculture. Together, we’re building a more resilient planet – one innovation at a time.

Overview

The Remediation Project Manager position is an exciting role in the FMC Corporate Environmental Remediation group for someone with a desire to manage environmental remediation projects. In this position, you will lead diverse teams, directing all phases of remediation projects at your assigned sites and support the teams involved in all remediation and construction projects. As a Remediation Project Manager, you will report to the Remediation Portfolio Manager.

Responsibilities

Develop and implement remedial strategies for assigned remediation sites safely and within budget.
Manage all projects to FMC safety standards and implement FMC’s culture of safety at all sites.
Select, manage and deploy diverse teams of specialists to direct all phases of site remediation projects, including field execution and construction, decontamination, and demolition activities.
Develop estimates for annual spend on projects. Meet project budgets, prepare all necessary authorization documents for spending and cost controls. Develop monthly forecasts to ensure tracking to budget.
Negotiate with governmental authorities the appropriate scope of work, the best alternatives for site remediation, and the level of FMC involvement at assigned remediation sites.
Retain and manage environmental consultants, laboratories and remedial contractors.
Prepare and present presentations to partners, including senior leadership, on project status, strategies, costs, progress, and new issues.
Communicate with management, other department members, other key FMC stakeholders (legal, procurement, finance, sustainability, etc.), and outside contractors on a variety of matters, including project status and other issues.
Critically review and edit for accuracy, style and content all reports, correspondence, field records, etc. which are prepared to document project work.
Identify new issues and trends on remediation project work and communicate relevant matters with the appropriate audience.
Occasional travel to project sites to actively manage and assist in the oversight of remedial construction and to participate in key regulatory and stakeholder meetings

Required Education

BS in Engineering, Natural Science, or related field

Qualifications

6+ years of environmental remediation and project management experience with 3+ years of experience working with federal or state environmental agencies on remediation issues. Sound understanding of USEPA and state agency policies and procedures, patterns of agency action and non-action, and typical responses.
Experience working with regulatory agencies, required. Previous work experience in an Industrial Corporate Environmental setting and/or working in a facility is preferred.
Previous responsibility for overseeing safety, technical, organizational management, and financial aspects of multiple simultaneous environmental projects.
Experience analyzing project requirements with important partners, evaluating feasibility, and developing a strategy for implementation.
Skill coordinating and overseeing safe field execution, construction, decontamination and demolition activities.
Experience managing projects, preferably >$5M annually, and developing project plans and schedules to implement and track project status.
Knowledge of environmental reserves and requirements imposed by government agencies.
Previous experience exercising practical judgment and ability to make data-driven decisions within context of defined processes.
Proficient in using common computer software, including: Microsoft Word®, Excel®, and PowerPoint® and SAP® (preferred).

Additional Preferred Qualifications

Technical knowledge and experience in complex environmental, occupational health, or worker safety subject areas in a manufacturing environment.
Direct management of environmental, health, and safety requirements, such as permit acquisition and compliance auditing.
Experience managing capital projects.
Experience with USEPA RCRA and CERCLA remediation programs
Professional licensure and certifications such as Professional Engineer (P.E.), Professional Geologist (P.G.), Licensed Site Remediation Professional (LSRP), Project Management Professional (PMP), or similar credentials are preferred but not required.
